content.value_statement: AI gateway teams need consistent policies for cost, safety, routing, and observability. This skill guides Azure API Management setup for governed AI access.
actual_capabilities: Provides Azure CLI patterns for creating AI backends in API Management.
Shows policies for token limits, semantic caching, token metrics, content safety, and rate limiting.
Explains managed identity authentication and RBAC role assignment patterns.
Includes troubleshooting checks for authentication, rate limits, cache behavior, content safety, and backend health.
Links SDK quick references for Azure Content Safety and Azure API Management.
limitations: Does not deploy Azure API Management by itself.
Requires Azure CLI and existing Azure resources for command examples.
Uses placeholders that must be replaced with tenant-specific values.
Does not validate organization-specific compliance or policy thresholds.

use_cases.title: Connect Azure OpenAI to APIM
use_cases.description: Add an Azure OpenAI backend with managed identity, RBAC access, and an imported OpenAPI surface.

use_cases.title: Control AI Gateway Costs
use_cases.description: Apply token limits, semantic caching, and token metrics to reduce spend and improve visibility.

use_cases.title: Protect Agent and Tool Traffic
use_cases.description: Configure content safety, jailbreak detection, and request rate limits for agent-facing APIs and MCP tools.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Gateway Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me get my Azure API Management gateway URL and list the configured AI backends. Use placeholder names for missing values.

prompt_templates.title: Add Azure OpenAI Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding an Azure OpenAI backend to API Management with managed identity and least-privilege RBAC.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Governance Policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an inbound policy plan for token limits, semantic caching, content safety, rate limits, and token metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Review Multi-Region Gateway
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my multi-region AI gateway design for backend selection, retry behavior, tenant isolation, MCP rate limits, and observability.

output_examples.input: I need to connect an Azure OpenAI resource to API Management.
output_examples.output: A setup plan covering managed identity, RBAC access, backend creation, API import, and policy placement.

output_examples.input: My AI gateway costs are rising, and I need better controls.
output_examples.output: A governance checklist for token limits, semantic cache settings, token metrics, and backend load distribution.

output_examples.input: I want safer agent traffic through APIM.
output_examples.output: Policy guidance for content safety, jailbreak detection, per-agent rate limiting, and troubleshooting blocked requests.

best_practices: Use managed identity and Azure RBAC for production backends.
Apply token limits, content safety, and metrics before forwarding AI traffic.
Test policies with placeholder values before applying them to shared gateways.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode secrets, subscription keys, or backend credentials in policies.
Do not use DefaultAzureCredential for production-hosted gateway workloads.
Do not enable semantic caching for streaming responses that require live output.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure API Management?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on AI gateway configuration after API Management exists.

faq.question: Can it configure Azure OpenAI backends?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Azure CLI and policy patterns for connecting Azure OpenAI through API Management.

faq.question: Does it support AI Foundry models?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns cover AI model backends that can be exposed through API Management.

faq.question: Can it help with content safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes APIM policy guidance for Azure AI Content Safety and jailbreak detection.

faq.question: Does it store or transmit credentials?
faq.answer: No. It recommends managed identity and placeholders instead of hardcoded secrets.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
